A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, Table 1, and appendices. V4 adds Appendix H; the subsequent appendices and figures can be matched despite renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Transformer training experiments, algorithmic phase diagrams, LIA fits, and mechanistic analyses, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds experiments evaluating Llama-3.1 models on Markov-sequence prediction in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The four analytic algorithms, Transformer training method, and constrained LIA objective remain unchanged. Llama models are additional experimental subjects; no new component of the proposed method is introduced.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds an instruction-conditioned test scenario, preceding digit sequences with natural-language prompts that disclose different amounts of Markov-process information. It reuses Appendix A.1's data-generating process and next-state prediction task, so the coverage extension is limited.

E2.justification: The four analytic reference algorithms and existing reconstruction and LIA controls are retained. The new Llama study uses the existing Uni-Inf and Bi-Inf references; it adds studied models rather than competing baselines for LIA.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces a separate pretrained-LLM evaluation protocol using Llama-3.1 at 8B, 70B, and 405B, 300 sampled sequences, three prompts, comma-separated digit tokens, and digit-restricted outputs. This substantially extends the experimental settings beyond the controlled trained Transformers; their original protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 38 tests sensitivity to instructions: generic continuation, an explicit Markov-process description, and an additional last-state dependency explanation. Existing architectural ablations, memorization analyses, attention analyses, distribution-shift tests, and LIA robustness checks are retained.

E5.justification: The existing evaluation repetitions and seed information, including 30 repetitions in Appendix A.3 and 30 seeds in Appendix D, are unchanged. Appendix H specifies 300 evaluation sequences but introduces no repeated-training protocol, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Figure 38 adds a substantive set of pretrained-LLM results: at longer contexts, Llama performance lies between Uni-Inf and Bi-Inf, larger models generally achieve lower KL, and explicit Markov instructions particularly improve 70B performance. The retained synthetic results, including Table 1 and the renumbered LIA validation plots, match across versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, algorithm equations, LIA formulation, and Bayesian interpretations are unchanged. V4 adds no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about finite Markov mixtures, four algorithmic phases, and competition explaining ICL phenomena. The Llama experiment does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H interprets instruction-dependent improvements as evidence that LLMs can incorporate natural-language descriptions into sequence prediction. It identifies reverse-engineering their algorithms through decomposition as future work. Existing mechanism interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V1 promises code release after peer review; v4 supplies a repository link and states that experiment and analysis code is available. Appendix H also documents NNsight/NDIF, exact prompts, sampling, and token handling. Existing training and implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references concerning Llama, Llama 3, NNsight/NDIF, prompt sensitivity, and scale-dependent ICL, supporting Appendix H. The existing research positioning and comparisons with earlier synthetic ICL studies remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 condenses the main evaluation description and moves its detail to Appendix A.3, inserts Appendix H, and updates subsequent cross-references. Publication headers, affiliation wording, and author contributions also change; most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds the three-panel Llama Figure 38 and retains the previous Figures 38–41 as Figures 39–42. Existing plots receive cleaner axes, labels, and legends, and Figure 4's Uni-Inf/Bi-Inf colors are corrected. The established displays and Table 1 remain structurally recognizable.

improvement.justification: Appendix H adds useful evidence that pretrained LLMs can learn the synthetic Markov task and respond to process descriptions, while the repository information improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited: the new experiment leaves LIA decomposition and competing algorithmic phases in Llama as future work, and the central scientific evidence and claims remain unchanged.
